simple.meaning: תַּחַשׁ (tachash) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a (clean) animal with fur , probably a species of antelope.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 25:5. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תַּחַשׁ (H8476) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תַּחַשׁ (tachash) / H8476 is traced through Exodus 25:5, Exodus 26:14, Exodus 35:7, Exodus 35:23 with generated occurrence evidence.

Everyone with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and sea cow hides, brought them.

the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, the covering of sea cow hides, the veil of the screen,

They shall put it and all its vessels within a covering of sealskin, and shall put it on the frame.
“On the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, and cover it with a covering of sealskin, and shall put in its poles.
“They shall take all the vessels of ministry with which they minister in the sanctuary, and put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of sealskin, and shall put them on the frame.

They shall put on it all its vessels with which they minister about it, the fire pans, the meat hooks, the shovels, and the basins—all the vessels of the altar; and they shall spread on it a covering of sealskin, and put in its poles.
they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, the covering of sealskin that is on it, the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,
I clothed you also with embroidered work, and put sealskin sandals on you. I dressed you with fine linen and covered you with silk.

definitions.full: H8476. tachash I. תַּ֫חַשׁ noun masculine ta—aš , a kind of leather or skin, and perhaps the animal yielding it (probably the dugong , compare Arabic dolphin , Thes 1500 Di-Ry Exod 25:5 Post Hast. DB BADGER ; Assyrian ta—šu (Dl Baer Ezech. xvi ), for which Dl Proi. 77 ff.; HWB 705 conjecture meaning sheep(skin) ; Bondi Egyptiaca 1 ff. compare Egyptian ¾µ´ , leather ; see summary of views M'Lean-Shiply Ency. Bib. BADGERS' SKINS ); — absolute ׳ת Num 4:6 +, תָּחַשׁ 4:8 +; plural תְּחָשִׁים Exod 25:5 +; — leather used for (woman's) sandals Ezek 16:10 ; elsewhere for cover of tabernacle Num 4:25 , ת ׳עוֺר 4:6 ; 4:8 ; 4:10 ; 4:11 ; 4:12 ; 4:14 , (הַ)תְּחָשִׁים עֹרֹת Exod 25:5 ; 26:14 ; 35:7 , 23 ; 36:19 ; 39:34 (all P).
